title: Minimum Operations to Achieve At Least K Peaks
summary: Given a circular array nums of length n, find the minimum operations to ensure at least k peaks.
statement: Given a circular array nums of length n, find the minimum operations to ensure at least k peaks. An index i is a peak if its value is strictly greater than its neighbors. You can increase any element by 1 in each operation. Return -1 if achieving k peaks is impossible.
constraints: nums is a nonempty circular array and k is nonnegative.
A peak is strictly greater than both circular neighbors; one operation increments one element.
Return the minimum operations producing at least k peaks, or -1 when impossible.
hints: Chosen peaks form an independent set on the cycle, with a fixed cost to raise each above its unchanged neighbors.
Split into cases excluding index zero or including it; inclusion excludes indices one and n-1.
Solve each remaining line with take/skip DP for exactly k selected indices.
Extra peaks are never cheaper than a k-subset, so exactly k suffices; the two cases cover every circular independent set.
editorial: Extra peaks are never cheaper than a k-subset, so exactly k suffices; the two cases cover every circular independent set.

tests.explanation: Raising either value two once creates a circular peak, so one operation is enough.
The only element is also both of its own neighbors and cannot be strictly greater, so return -1.
